schemaVersion: Ehel Intensive English Course Manifest v1.0
subject: English
audience: Adult ESL learners of any first language, beginner upwards, studying intensively and mostly alone. No child-world, and no task that assumes a particular adult life (a job, a car, a home, children or papers): where a task needs one, the learner may invent it.

cefr.name: Common European Framework of Reference for Languages
cefr.role: Defines what a learner can DO at the end of each level, and therefore what each level's exit assessment tests. This is the framework the course reports against.
cefr.structure: Three levels, and the course ENDS at B1. Level 1 (0057 Stages 1-3) runs Pre-A1 to A1, Level 2 (0057 Stages 4-6) A1 to A2, and Level 3 (0876 Stages 7-9) A2 to B1. Each opens where the one below it exits, which is the property the 2026-09-12 rebuild existed to restore — before it, Level 1 exited at A1 and Level 2 opened at B1, so nothing taught the two levels between them. See whyTheCourseStopsAtB1.

cambridge.name: Cambridge Primary English as a Second Language 0057; Cambridge Primary English 0058; Cambridge Lower Secondary English 0861
cambridge.role: 0057 is the CONTRACT for Levels 1 and 2: every 0057 objective of a level's stages is placed in exactly one unit (plan field `esl`), and the build fails a unit whose outcomes do not cite its placed objectives. 0058 is an optional literacy cross-reference. Level 3 and above keep the 0058 / 0861 codes of the school units they were compressed from.

frameworks.howTheyRelate: They are not the same axis. A Cambridge stage supplies the language sequence; CEFR sets the target and is recorded separately for each skill as a language-support measure. Level 1 follows the owner's planning note (Stages 1-3, Pre-A1 to A1) and Level 2 will follow Stages 4-6 (A1 to A2). Completing a level does not by itself establish a CEFR level: reading, writing, listening and speaking are assessed separately and may be at different levels.

level.label: Intro — Starting English
level.cefrName: Pre-A1, from no English at all

cefrBands.cefrName: Pre-A1, from no English at all
cefrBands.canDo: Understand and say greetings, your own name, numbers and the words for people, things and places around you; copy the 26 letters and begin to read short familiar words.

level.exitDescriptor: Exits ready for Level 1 Unit 0. Can hold a pen and copy the 26 letters in both forms, say the alphabet, spell their own name, count to twenty, and ask and answer about people, things, places, food, health and work in two- and three-word turns. Begins to blend sounds into short words.
level.exitAssessment: A Pre-A1 check at the end of Unit 16, reported per skill and never as one grade. It is not a barrier: Level 1 Unit 0 re-teaches the letters and blending, so a learner may move on before passing it.
